written: 2026-10-27 by hack-lab (workload kernelbench-gb10); clock lock 2200 -> 2000 MHz on 2026-10-29

service.access: ${SMA_HOST} only (tailnet tag kernelbench-client, whose only grant is this service), plus the lab owner; no key
service.evaluates: one kernel at a time; the GPU belongs to this service alone (a Kubernetes DRA claim), and the host's own model slot is off

gpu.name: NVIDIA GB10
gpu.memory: 121 GB unified LPDDR5X shared with the CPU (273 GB/s, NVIDIA's spec); no separate GPU memory

clock_lock.how: a systemd unit at boot: nvidia-smi --persistence-mode=1, then --lock-gpu-clocks=2000,2000 (min = max)
clock_lock.why: repeatable timings: unlocked, the clock moves with temperature and the power cap. Since 2026-10-29 every DGX Spark in the lab runs locked at 2000 MHz (the lab owner: similar performance on all three, cooler and longer-lived)
clock_lock.memory_clock: not reported or settable on the GB10

measured_unlocked.load: fp32 8192x8192 matmul plus a 4 GiB elementwise loop, 90 s
measured_unlocked.event_reasons: 0x0 and 0x4 (SW power cap) now and then

gpu.lock_cost: Against 2200 MHz: 2.4% longer (geometric mean over 249 problems; median 1.3%). 2200 MHz against unlocked: Level 1 2.6% longer (geometric mean; median 0.3%)

measured_locked_2200.event_reasons: 0x0, with 0x4 now and then without moving the clock

measured_locked_2000.load: the KernelBench baselines below (levels 1-3, one job), sampled every 15 s

software.torch_cuda_arch_list: 12.1 (kernels build for sm_121; PyTorch's own kernels are sm_120, which run on 12.1, so its startup warning is harmless)
software.not_installed: LiteLLM and the OpenAI client (KernelBench imports them for generation, which the service never does; stubs take their names)
software.extra_python_packages: einops 0.8.1 (Level 3's Mamba2 problems 48 and 49 import it), numpy 2.3.5, ninja 1.13.0; the problems need nothing else beyond torch and the standard library

container.memory_rules: a worker is stopped when the container's own memory passes 94 GiB (2 GiB short of the limit, which would kill the whole container), or when the machine's available memory falls below 8 GiB: on unified memory the GPU's allocations come from the machine's RAM and are not charged to the container
container.network: none (no egress; only the node's tailnet serve reaches it)
container.user: uid 10001, no capabilities, Pod Security restricted, no Kubernetes token
container.sandbox: each kernel in its own process under Landlock ABI 7 (host kernel 6.17): writes only its scratch folder, /dev and its own /proc entry; no TCP; signals and abstract sockets scoped to itself
